note: Level 1, both label levels read in the two .sav files that feed this table (files reused from the batch_650 cache; full sha256 match the batch_650 record). Code derivation (data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py, interest.csv spec: interest{i} -> interest{i} for s1c and s2 only, no flip): item IS the source column name in both studies, so exempt from Step 5b and no verification files. Scope: this is NOT wallace_2026_interest_org (interestwork_MCM / interest from S1a/S1b/S2a/S2b/S2c, agree-disagree anchored), which is a separate table and untouched here. PER-STUDY VARIANTS: live cov_study 1 = Study 2 (838 ids), 4 = S1c (796). All three items are worded differently in each study (Study 2 about taking a class taught by / with the professor; S1c about working at a place like MCM Consulting), so following the batch_644-650 convention item_text carries both verbatim variable labels prefixed 'Study 2 (cov_study = 1): ' / 'Study S1c (cov_study = 4): ' joined by ' | ' (prefixes and separator are IRW's; wording after each prefix is the label verbatim). OPTIONS: every item in both studies has value labels 1='1 - not at all', 7='7 - extremely', 2-6 carry only their own digit; digit prefixes stripped (lowercase kept as in the labels) and 2-6 left blank. NO RECODE (no itemcov_recoded column in the live table; both studies print the same 1 = not at all order). Route 9: all 6 study x item count vectors match source = live exactly: Study 2 interest1 135/87/86/106/163/146/115, interest2 153/98/84/115/147/128/113, interest3 121/83/85/121/133/153/142; S1c interest1 45/36/51/111/191/209/153, interest2 47/46/58/110/196/182/157, interest3 40/29/38/104/156/234/195. Direction cross-check: growth-mindset condition (treat=1) has HIGHER mean interest than fixed (treat=0) in both studies (Study 2 5.5 vs 2.8, S1c 5.5 vs 4.6), consistent with 1 = not at all ... 7 = extremely. No instructions text in either .sav or .sps; left blank. Rights: study-authored items, no stated restriction located (silence = permission).
public_note: Items were worded for a different target in each pooled study (taking a class with a professor in Study 2, cov_study = 1; working at MCM Consulting in Study S1c, cov_study = 4), so item_text gives both wordings labelled by study; responses run 1 = not at all to 7 = extremely, the opposite direction from the agree-disagree wallace_2026_interest_org table.
